browserWorkerEvidence.command: npm run test:e2e -- --grep connections readiness records reproducible large-fixture browser timing --repeat-each=3
browserWorkerEvidence.environment: Playwright Chromium; desktop and Pixel 7-equivalent mobile projects; service worker prepared before context is taken offline
browserWorkerEvidence.warmup: Each isolated E2E loads the app and waits for offline readiness before measurement.
browserWorkerEvidence.outlierPolicy: No sample removed; p95 is the maximum of three samples.

acceptedWorkerReferenceRatios.note: This is the previously accepted worker evidence rather than a same-process baseline. Same-process ELK timing ratios are in routeEvidence.

bundleComparison.method: Same-host production builds at the branch point and worktree, using the same node_modules and gzip -c.

compatibility.offline: pass: the existing pre-cached ELK worker reaches ready while Playwright context is offline; no network route fallback was added
compatibility.accessibility: pass: semantic directed-edge list cardinality and labels remain independent of visual port sides; node buttons retain focus and activation
compatibility.camera: pass: layout remains a graph/metric-keyed worker result; the gesture E2E asserts unchanged node/edge geometry during pan, pinch, cancel, and lost capture

visual.note: Issue #59 changes geometry only. CSS, tokens, edge halo, marker, and theme logic are byte-identical, so existing dark captures are reused for the dark-style axis while new desktop/mobile light captures review the changed production layout.

result: pass: the production default uses one offline ELK layout with free side selection, keeps all hard and semantic contracts, passes the representative performance thresholds, and adds 40 gzip bytes without a new dependency
